chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

About a man: is it permissible for him to look at his wife when she dies, or to wash her if there is no one with her to wash her? And about a woman: may she look at the like of that from her husband when he dies? So he said:
There is no harm in that. Rather, it is only the woman’s family who do that, out of dislike that her husband should look at something of her that they would dislike.

key_terms.أَيَصْلُحُ: whether it is permissible or proper
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection
key_terms.يَغْسِلُهَا: to wash her body for the deceased’s ghusl

ai.seo_question: Can a husband or wife look at or wash their spouse after death in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states that there is no problem with a husband looking at or washing his wife after her death if no one else is available, and likewise for a wife with her husband. It also notes that reluctance in such cases may come from the woman’s family, not from a prohibition in itself.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.398 - Abdullah ibn Sinan asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about whether it is permissible for a man to look at his wife when She dies or to wash her if there is no one else to wash her, and likewise, if a woman can do the same for her husband when he dies. Imam (as) replied:
"There is no issue with that.
It is usually the woman's family who may dislike her husband seeing something he would dislike about her."
